children.note: The top stage of basic education under CBC, after junior school.
Senior school lasts three years: Grade 10, Grade 11 and Grade 12.

manas.q: Which grades make up senior school?

children.note: The 2019 curriculum framework places senior school learners at about 16 to 18 years old. Some learners will be younger or older.

manas.q: What ages does the 2019 framework give for senior school?

children.note: Learners move up from junior school after Grade 9. Grade 10 under CBC started in 2026.
Unlike earlier levels, each learner follows one pathway that matches their interests, strengths and hoped-for careers.

manas.q: What is a pathway in senior school?

children.topic: A track is a group of subjects
children.note: Inside each pathway are tracks. A track is a combination of related subjects, for example Pure Sciences inside STEM.

manas.q: What is a track in senior school?

children.note: The three pathways are STEM, Social Sciences, and Arts and Sports Science.

manas.q: Name the three senior school pathways.

children.note: Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics. For learners who enjoy numbers, experiments, machines, computers and farming.
Science and maths studied in depth, the base for medicine, engineering and research. Subjects: Core Mathematics, Essential Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, General Science.

manas.q: Which STEM track includes Biology, Chemistry and Physics?

children.note: Science used in daily life: growing food, computers and running a healthy home. Subjects: Agriculture, Computer Studies, Home Science, Information Communication Technology.

manas.q: Which STEM track includes Agriculture and Computer Studies?

children.note: Hands-on skills for building, fixing and making things. Subjects: Aviation, Building Construction, Electricity, Metal Work, Power Mechanics, Woodwork, Media Technology, Marine & Fisheries.

manas.q: Name two subjects in the Technical Studies track.

children.note: The course book lists show both Core Mathematics and Essential Mathematics. Ask your school which one fits your child's track.

manas.q: What two kinds of mathematics appear in the STEM course lists?

children.note: For learners who enjoy languages, reading, people, history, places, faith and business.
Reading, writing, speaking and enjoying stories in Kenyan and foreign languages. Subjects: English, Literature in English, Kiswahili, Fasihi ya Kiswahili, Arabic, French, German (Grade 11 list only).

manas.q: Which Social Sciences track includes Literature in English and Fasihi ya Kiswahili?

children.note: How people live, believe, govern, trade and look after places. Subjects: Christian Religious Education (CRE), Islamic Religious Education (IRE), Community Service Learning, History & Citizenship, Geography, Business Studies, Life Skills (Grade 11 list only).

manas.q: Which track includes History & Citizenship, Geography and Business Studies?

children.note: For learners with talent and love for music, drama, art, sport and fitness.
Creating and performing: songs, dance, plays, films and visual art. Subjects: Music and Dance, Theatre and Film, Fine Arts.

manas.q: Name the three subjects in the Arts track.

children.note: How the body moves, trains and stays healthy, plus playing and organising sport. Subjects: Sports and Recreation, Physical Education.

manas.q: Which two subjects make up the Sports Science track?

children.note: The 2019 framework used older wording, including a talent pathway for drama, music and dance. Today's lists call it Arts and Sports Science.
Choosing well starts with the learner, not with what friends or neighbours pick. Talk it through as a family.
Ask: What do you enjoy doing even when nobody tells you to? Fixing a radio, reading novels, drawing, playing football?

manas.q: What is the first thing to look at when choosing a pathway?

children.note: Ask: Which learning areas come easily? What do teachers praise? Junior school reports and projects give clues.
Ask: What kind of work do you picture yourself doing? Then check which pathway leads there.

children.topic: Ask: what do I want to learn more of?
children.note: A pathway means more time on certain subjects. Pick the ones the learner is happy to study deeply for three years.

children.topic: Ask: which schools offer this track?
children.note: Not every school offers every track or subject. Check what nearby schools offer before deciding.

manas.q: Does every school offer every track?

children.note: Junior school teachers know your child's work. Ask them which pathway they would suggest and why.

children.topic: Talk to people in real jobs
children.note: A nurse, mechanic, accountant or musician in your area can explain what their work is really like.
A pathway is not better because it sounds important. The right one is where your child will grow and stay motivated.
Ask your school how and when pathway and school choices are made and what deadlines apply. Rules may change each year.

children.topic: KJSEA gives a pathway strength score
children.note: KNEC does not add KJSEA subjects into one total. Instead a formula gives a strength value from 0 to 75 for each pathway — the higher, the stronger the sign of potential there.

manas.q: What range does the KJSEA pathway strength value use?

children.note: KNEC's September 2025 circular: Grade 9 learners are placed into the three pathways from January 2026 on potential, achievements and aspirations.
Because talent in music, dance, theatre, visual arts and sport is hard to see in written tests, junior school teachers nominate learners on a Ministry tool for the Arts and Sports Science pathway.

manas.q: How are learners identified for the Arts and Sports Science pathway?

children.note: General examples only. Many careers welcome learners from more than one pathway.
Doctors, nurses, engineers, computer experts, farmers and agronomists, builders, electricians, mechanics, pilots and media technicians.

manas.q: Give three career areas STEM can lead to.

children.note: Lawyers, teachers, journalists, translators, faith leaders, historians, geographers, traders, accountants and community workers.

children.topic: Arts and Sports Science: creative, sports
children.note: Musicians, actors, filmmakers, artists, designers, coaches, PE teachers, fitness trainers and sports managers.
Good communication, teamwork and problem solving help in every job, whichever pathway a learner takes.
Learning by helping the community, then reflecting on it in class.
Learners use what they know to meet a real need in the community, working with community partners, then think back on what they learned.

manas.q: What is community service learning?

children.note: In senior school, Community Service Learning appears as a subject in the Humanities & Business Studies track course lists.

manas.q: In which senior school track is Community Service Learning listed?

children.note: A clean-up of the local market, a tree-planting day, helping at a children's home, or teaching younger children to read.

children.topic: Ask how your school runs it
children.note: How projects are chosen, recorded and assessed may differ. Check with your school.
The seven core competencies and national values continue in senior school, at a more grown-up level.
Example: planning and testing a better irrigation idea for a school shamba.
Example: a group presenting findings to the class or community.
Example: using a computer to research, present data or edit a short film safely.
Example: learning how local leaders are chosen and taking part in a community project.
Believing you can succeed and knowing how to study on your own, key skills for university and work.
Shown by meeting deadlines, treating others well and doing your own work.
How learning is checked in senior school. KNEC set the rules in a circular to senior schools on 8 May 2026 (read 4 Nov 2026). Your school has the details.
Teachers keep checking learning through tasks, projects, practicals, presentations and tests during the year.
KNEC says Grade 10 SBAs are projects, practicals and written tests, run by the school and scored on the KNEC CBA portal. (KNEC, read 4 Nov 2026 — check the current rule.)

manas.q: What three kinds of task make up Grade 10 school-based assessments?

children.note: In 2026 the Grade 10 projects and practicals ran between May and September. Dates can change each year — ask the school.
The 2026 written tests were to be finished by 15 October, in Term III. (KNEC, read 4 Nov 2026 — check the current rule.)

children.topic: Scores go to the CBA portal
children.note: Schools upload scores and keep evidence of each learner's work. Keep your child's project files safe.

children.topic: Final exam: KCBE at end of Grade 12
children.note: KNEC calls the final reporting the Kenya Certificate of Basic Education (KCBE) examination. It combines school-based and summative (final) assessment. (KNEC, read 4 Nov 2026 — check the current rule.)

manas.q: What does KCBE stand for?

children.note: KNEC's May 2026 circular: Grade 10 SBA 15%, Grade 11 SBA 15%, Grade 12 summative assessment 70% of the final subject score. (KNEC, read 4 Nov 2026 — check the current rule.)

manas.q: What share of the final KCBE subject score comes from Grade 12?

children.note: Because 15% of the final score is earned in Grade 10, steady work from the first year matters — it is not only about the last exam.
If a learner scores 80 in Grade 10 SBA, 70 in Grade 11 SBA and 60 in the Grade 12 exam: 0.15×80 + 0.15×70 + 0.70×60 = 12 + 10.5 + 42 = 64.5.

manas.q: A learner has SBA 80 (G10), 70 (G11) and exam 60 (G12). Final score?

children.topic: Pilot of the final exam in 2027
children.note: KNEC planned to pilot the senior school summative assessment in 2027, when the first CBC cohort is in Grade 11. The first full KCBE would follow in Grade 12. (KNEC, read 4 Nov 2026 — check the current rule.)
Each learner keeps the assessment number given at Grade 3 right through to Grade 12. Schools used it to register Grade 10 learners in 2026.

manas.q: From which grade does a learner's KNEC assessment number come?

children.topic: KJSEA report needed to join Grade 10
children.note: Learners had to present their KJSEA performance report, stamped by the junior school head, to be registered in senior school.
KNEC wrote a Competency Based Assessment Framework for Senior School and asked schools to share it with teachers. Ask the school for it if you want the full rules.
Details not yet found on official pages (checked again 4 Nov 2026). Always confirm with your school.
The course book lists do not say which senior school subjects every learner must take. Check with your school.

manas.q: Do the KICD course lists show which senior school subjects are compulsory?

children.topic: How many subjects each learner takes
children.note: The number of subjects per learner was not confirmed. Check with your school.
Whether and how a learner can switch pathway or track later was not confirmed. Ask your school.
Entry rules for courses after CBC were not confirmed. Check with universities and colleges closer to the time.
On 4 Nov 2026 KNEC's circular confirmed the name Kenya Certificate of Basic Education (KCBE) and the 15/15/70 split — see the Assessment branch.
Senior school opens several doors. There is no single right route.
Degree courses such as medicine, law, engineering or education. Check each course's requirements.
Technical and vocational colleges teach practical trades and diplomas, such as electrical work, plumbing, catering or ICT.

manas.q: What do TVET colleges teach?

children.note: Some learners start work, an apprenticeship or their own small business, using skills from their track.
Short courses, online learning and on-the-job training help people grow throughout their careers.
Small, cheap actions at home make a big difference in these years.
Ask your teen what they enjoy and hope for, and listen fully before giving your view.
A visit to a garage, clinic, farm, studio or office helps a teen see what a job looks like.
Agree a quiet study time and place at home, even a corner of the kitchen table.

children.topic: Stay in touch with the school
children.note: Attend meetings and read reports. Ask teachers how your child is doing in their track.
Praise your teen for helping neighbours, the church, mosque or community group.
Sleep, food, rest and someone to talk to matter as much as marks.
Rely on your school, KICD and KNEC rather than rumours on social media.
